question: Which thermostable enzyme hydrolyses starch during the cooking of sweet potatoes?
solution:
The correct answer is __**β-amylase**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] __Key Points__

• **β-amylase** is an enzyme that is involved in the hydrolysis of starch, converting it into maltose and dextrin.

• It is a thermostable enzyme, meaning it can function effectively at high temperatures, such as those encountered during cooking.

• This enzyme is particularly important in the cooking and processing of sweet potatoes, as it helps in breaking down starch into simpler sugars, enhancing the sweetness and digestibility of the cooked product.
